items.title: The one-dimensional endpoint estimate on a bounded interval
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice through the ACL interface of [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]]. Let $I=(a,b)$ be a bounded open interval, $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ with weak derivative $u'$ and unique absolutely continuous representative $u^*$ ([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]]). Then for every $0<\varepsilon<b-a$: (i) if $1<p<\infty$, $|u^*(a)|^p\le 2^{p-1}\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^{p-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\bigr)$, and the same inequality holds at $b$ with $(b-\varepsilon,b)$; (ii) if $p=1$, $|u^*(a)|\le\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|+\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|$, and likewise at $b$. The endpoint values are those of the absolutely continuous representative and do not depend on the chosen representative of the class.
items.strategy: For a.e. $t\in(a,a+\varepsilon)$ the absolutely continuous representative satisfies $u^*(a)-u^*(t)=-\int_a^t u'$, hence $|u^*(a)|\le|u^*(t)|+\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|$. For $p>1$ raise this to the $p$-th power with $|x+y|^p\le 2^{p-1}(|x|^p+|y|^p)$, integrate in $t$ over $(a,a+\varepsilon)$, divide by $\varepsilon$, and bound $\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|\bigr)^p=\varepsilon\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|\bigr)^p\le\varepsilon^p\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p$ by Holder. For $p=1$ integrate the unsquared inequality. The capital-$C$ form used later is $\varepsilon|u^*(a)|^p\le C_p\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^p\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\bigr)$. The ACL and FTC interfaces carry the Axiom of Choice; no further choice is used.

items.title: The half-space trace estimate and the half-space trace operator
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $H=\{x=(x',x_n)\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ with $\partial H=\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}$. (i) For every $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)$ with compact support, the classical boundary function $g=u(\cdot,0)$ satisfies $|g(x')|^p\le p\int_0^\infty|u(x',t)|^{p-1}\,|\partial_nu(x',t)|\,dt$ for a.e. $x'\in\mathbb R^d$, hence $\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}^p\le p\,\|u\|_{L^p(H)}^{p-1}\|\partial_nu\|_{L^p(H)}\le p\,\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p$. For every $h>0$ the strip form $h\,|g(x')|^p\le C_p\bigl(\int_0^h|u(x',t)|^pdt+h^p\int_0^h|\partial_nu(x',t)|^pdt\bigr)$ holds for a.e. $x'$. (ii) There is a unique bounded linear operator $T_+:W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)\to L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$ with $T_+u=u(\cdot,0)$ for every compactly supported $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H)$, and $\|T_+u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}\le C(n,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$; it is the unique bounded extension of classical restriction, and $T_+u$ depends only on the a.e. class of $u$.
items.strategy: For (i), fix a representative continuous on $\overline H$; for a.e. $x'$ the section $t\mapsto u(x',t)$ is absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$ by the ACL theorem, and since $u$ has compact support, $|g(x')|^p=-\int_0^\infty\partial_t(|u(x',t)|^p)\,dt=-p\int_0^\infty|u|^{p-2}\operatorname{Re}(\overline u\,\partial_nu)dt\le p\int_0^\infty|u|^{p-1}|\partial_nu|\,dt$. Integrate in $x'$, apply Holder with exponents $p/(p-1)$ and $p$, and use $\|\partial_nu\|_p\le\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$. The strip form integrates the one-dimensional endpoint estimate [[lem-one-dimensional-sobolev-endpoint-estimate]] along the normal section. For (ii), classical restriction is defined on compactly supported smooth functions and is uniformly bounded by (i); that subspace is dense in $W^{1,p}(H)$ because a cutoff in $|x|$ reduces to the bounded domains $H\cap B_R$, where [[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]] applies. Apply the bounded-extension property of a dense subspace ([[thm-completion-universal-property-for-bounded-linear-maps]]); uniqueness is immediate. The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density interface used to reach all classes.

items.title: The $L^p$ trace operator on a bounded $C^1$ domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain in the graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\partial\Omega$ carry the chart-independent surface measure of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]], let $1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then there is a unique bounded linear operator $T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\to L^p(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $Tu=u|_{\partial\Omega}$ for every $u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and it satisfies $\|Tu\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. On each boundary chart the operator is the flat half-space trace $T_+$ transported by the flattening diffeomorphism, and the chartwise definitions agree on overlaps; uniqueness holds because two bounded operators agreeing on the dense subspace $C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ are equal.
items.strategy: Choose the finite boundary atlas and the subordinate finite ambient partition $\chi_j$ of [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]], and write $u=\sum_j\chi_ju$ for $u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$. Every piece is supported in one chart; flattening it with the $C^1$ chart and [[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]] gives a compactly supported function in $W^{1,p}(H)$, to which the flat estimate of [[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]] applies. Summing the finitely many chartwise boundary $L^p$ norms gives the global bound because the transported boundary integrals agree up to the chart Jacobian ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]], [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]). The classical restriction operator is therefore uniformly bounded on the dense subspace $C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]) and extends uniquely to a bounded operator on $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ ([[thm-completion-universal-property-for-bounded-linear-maps]]). Well-definedness on classes: the boundary measure is chart independent and null sets in $\Omega$ do not affect the boundary integrals. The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density and flattening interfaces; the finite cover and partition use no further choice.

items.title: The trace agrees with classical restriction for continuous Sobolev functions
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1\le p<\infty$, and let $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ admit a representative $\tilde u\in C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then, with $T$ the trace operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], $Tu=\tilde u|_{\partial\Omega}$ in $L^p(\partial\Omega)$; in particular $Tu=0$ whenever such a representative vanishes on $\partial\Omega$. Two representatives continuous on $\overline\Omega$ of the same class have the same restriction to $\partial\Omega$.
items.strategy: The class $u$ has the representative $\tilde u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and the defining property of $T$ in [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] is exactly that the trace of such a class is its classical restriction. If $\tilde u$ vanishes on $\partial\Omega$, its classical restriction is the zero class of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$. The restriction of a function continuous on the compact set $\overline\Omega$ is determined by the function, so two such representatives agree on $\partial\Omega$. No choice beyond the cited trace interface is used.

items.title: The trace commutes with smooth cutoffs and is chart local
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1\le p<\infty$, and let $T$ be the trace operator of
[[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]].

(i) If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$, then
$T(\eta u)=(\eta|_{\partial\Omega})\,Tu$ in $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ for every
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and
$\|T(\eta u)\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C_\eta\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$.

(ii) If $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ is a bounded $C^1$ domain and
$\partial\Omega\cap\partial\Omega'$ is relatively open in $\partial\Omega$,
then $(Tu)|_{\partial\Omega\cap\partial\Omega'}=T_{\Omega'}(u|_{\Omega'})$
a.e. for every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, where $T_{\Omega'}$ is the trace
operator relative to $\Omega'$; in particular the trace is local and
compatible with restrictions to subdomains.

(iii) If a boundary chart $\Phi$ flattens a neighbourhood of a boundary point,
then for $u$ supported in a compact ambient patch inside that chart the transported trace
equals $T_+$ of the zero-extended flattened function after reflecting $t\mapsto-t$ and the corresponding boundary $L^p$ norms
agree up to the chart Jacobian.
items.strategy: Density of ambient smooth restrictions and boundedness give multiplicativity and locality for bounded C1 subdomains. Localise approximants by a fixed ambient cutoff, flatten and reflect, extend across artificial chart edges using the support margin, and pass to the limit; C1 pullbacks need only be continuous Sobolev functions.

items.title: The Gauss-Green integration-by-parts formula with Sobolev traces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$,
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, $v\in W^{1,p'}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let
$T$ be the trace of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with
$\nu$ the outward normal of
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Then for
every $i=1,\dots,n$,
$$\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv\,dx=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\,\nu_i\,dS,$$
and all three integrals are finite. If $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the
boundary term is the classical $\int_{\partial\Omega}uv\,\nu_i\,dS$ of the
divergence theorem
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to the
field $uv\,e_i$; if in addition $Tu=\partial_\nu w$ on $\partial\Omega$ for a specified $w\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the boundary term is $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\partial_\nu w)(Tv)\nu_i\,dS$. The normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]] is defined on the boundary, and this extra identity is an assumption, not an interior substitution.
items.strategy: For $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ the identity is the divergence theorem applied to the field $uv\,e_i$ on the bounded $C^1$ domain. For general $u,v$ choose $u_k\to u$ in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ and $v_k\to v$ in $W^{1,p'}(\Omega)$ with $u_k,v_k$ restrictions of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ functions ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]), so that $Tu_k\to Tu$ and $Tv_k\to Tv$ in the respective boundary $L^p$ spaces. The volume pairings converge by Holder, $\int_\Omega|u_k\partial_iv_k-u\partial_iv|\le\|u_k-u\|_p\|\partial_iv_k\|_{p'}+\|u\|_p\|\partial_iv_k-\partial_iv\|_{p'}\to0$, and the boundary pairings converge by Holder on $\partial\Omega$ with exponents $p,p'$ ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]), the boundary measure being finite. All boundary terms are in $L^1(\partial\Omega)$ since $Tu\in L^p$ and $Tv\in L^{p'}$. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density and trace interfaces.

items.title: The kernel of the trace is the closure of the test functions
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain and $1\le p<\infty$. Then the kernel of the trace operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] equals the zero-boundary Sobolev space: $\{u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega):Tu=0\}=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, the $W^{1,p}$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]).
items.strategy: Continuity proves the test-closure inclusion. For zero flat trace, direct integration on smooth approximants proves weak derivatives of zero extension. Translate inward and mollify inside the half-space. Localise before C1 pullback, then mollify each compact interior Sobolev pullback to obtain smooth tests. Treat the interior residual by bounded-domain compact support.

items.title: The Gagliardo--Slobodeckij space on Euclidean space
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice for the measure interfaces. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$, $1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. For a measurable $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb K$ put $[g]_{s,p}:=\bigl(\int_{\mathbb R^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|g(x)-g(y)|^p|x-y|^{-d-sp}\,dx\,dy\bigr)^{1/p}\in[0,\infty]$, with the integrand understood as $0$ on the diagonal $x=y$. The Gagliardo-Slobodeckij space is $W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K):=\{g\in L^p(\mathbb R^d):[g]_{s,p}<\infty\}$, normed by $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}}:=\|g\|_{L^p}+[g]_{s,p}$. The seminorm and the space are meant to depend only on the almost-everywhere class; representative independence is recorded as the first clause of the well-definedness lemma on this page. On this page the exponent used is $s=\theta:=1-1/p\in(0,1)$, which is the trace exponent for $1<p<\infty$.
items.strategy: Unpack the double integral as an integral over the completed product measure on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ ([[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]); the diagonal is a null set, so the convention is harmless, and the integral is a nonnegative extended integral of a measurable function ([[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]). Membership and norm are stated on classes ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]); representative independence is not assumed here but proved as the first clause of [[lem-slobodeckij-seminorm-is-well-defined]]. Only the countable-choice measure interfaces are used; the definition itself is choice free.

items.title: Well-definedness of the Slobodeckij seminorm and norm
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. (i) If $g=h$ almost everywhere then $[g]_{s,p}=[h]_{s,p}$ (both possibly infinite). (ii) The extended quantity $[\cdot]_{s,p}$ is a seminorm: $[\lambda g]_{s,p}=|\lambda|[g]_{s,p}$ and $[f+g]_{s,p}\le[f]_{s,p}+[g]_{s,p}$ for all measurable $f,g$. (iii) If $g\in L^p(\mathbb R^d)$ and $[g]_{s,p}=0$, then $g=0$ a.e.; hence $\|\cdot\|_{W^{s,p}}$ is a norm and $W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ is a vector space. On a set of finite measure the seminorm vanishes on constants, so it is only definite modulo constants there; adding the $L^p$ term removes that ambiguity, and on $\mathbb R^d$ with $p<\infty$ no nonzero constant is in $L^p$.
items.strategy: (i) The difference $g-h$ vanishes outside a null set $N$; then $(g(x)-g(y))-(h(x)-h(y))=0$ whenever $x,y\notin N$, and $(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d)\setminus(N\times N)$ is null-complemented by Tonelli. (ii) Additivity of the integrand and Minkowski's integral inequality [[thm-minkowski-integral-inequality]] applied twice, first in $y$ and then in $x$, give the triangle inequality; homogeneity is immediate. (iii) If $[g]=0$ then $|g(x)-g(y)|^p=0$ for a.e. pair, hence by Fubini for a.e. $x$ for a.e. $y$; fix such an $x$ outside the exceptional set and conclude $g(y)=g(x)$ for a.e. $y$, so $g$ is a.e. constant; since $g\in L^p$ and $\mathbb R^d$ has infinite measure, the constant is $0$ ([[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]] gives the a.e.-zero conclusion after integrating $|g|^p$). Only countable-choice measure interfaces are used.

items.title: The coordinate-direction form of the Slobodeckij seminorm
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$, $1\le p<\infty$, and let $g$ be measurable. Then, with $e_1,\dots,e_d$ the canonical basis, $[g]_{s,p}^p\asymp_{d,p,s}\sum_{i=1}^d\int_0^\infty h^{-1-sp}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|g(x+he_i)-g(x)|^p\,dx\,dh$, in the sense that both sides are finite simultaneously and the two quantities are comparable by constants depending only on $d,p,s$. For the trace exponent $s=\theta=1-1/p$ the weight is $h^{-p}$, because $1+p\theta=p$.
items.strategy: Use a Borel representative and polar coordinates for extended nonnegative integrals. Telescope general increments along coordinate directions for one bound; average a pointwise triangle inequality against fixed compact smooth probability densities for the reverse bound, without integrating g itself.

items.title: The Hardy inequality for the averaging operator on the half-line
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $f:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable, with
$Hf(t):=t^{-1}\int_0^t f(s)\,ds$. Then
$$\Bigl(\int_0^\infty\bigl(Hf(t)\bigr)^p\,dt\Bigr)^{1/p}\le\frac{p}{p-1}\Bigl(\int_0^\infty f(s)^p\,ds\Bigr)^{1/p},$$
equivalently
$$\int_0^\infty t^{-p}\Bigl(\int_0^t f(s)\,ds\Bigr)^pdt\le\Bigl(\frac{p}{p-1}\Bigr)^p\int_0^\infty f(s)^p\,ds,$$
where both sides are extended nonnegative integrals and $+\infty$ is allowed on
either side. The constant $p/(p-1)$ is sharp: for every $c<p/(p-1)$ there is a
measurable $f$ with $\|Hf\|_{L^p}>c\|f\|_{L^p}$. If $f$ is supported in
$(0,T)$ for some $0<T<\infty$, then the same inequality holds on $(0,T)$,
$$\int_0^T t^{-p}\Bigl(\int_0^t f(s)\,ds\Bigr)^pdt\le\Bigl(\frac{p}{p-1}\Bigr)^p\int_0^T f(s)^p\,ds,$$
with the same constant.
items.strategy: Truncate monotonically to bounded compactly supported data, establish finite dual-test integral, bound the tail-dual operator by Minkowski, and obtain sharpness with t^(-1/p) on (1,R) and successive logarithmic limits. Restrict the full estimate for the interval case.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, and let $\psi\in C_c(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\psi=0$. For $t>0$ put $\psi_t(y)=t^{-d}\psi(y/t)$. items.title: The fractional Sobolev space on a compact $C^1$ boundary
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the boundary conventions of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Fix a finite family of boundary charts $\Phi_j:U_j\to V_j$, whose restrictions parametrise $\partial\Omega\cap U_j$ over open sets of $\mathbb R^{n-1}$, and a subordinate finite ambient partition $\chi_j$ ([[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]]). For a Borel function $g:\partial\Omega\to\mathbb K$ set $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega)}:=\sum_j\|(\chi_jg)\circ\Phi_j^{-1}\|_{W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^{n-1})}$, where the chart representation is taken in graph coordinates. Then $W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the set of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ classes with finite norm. The definition is independent of the atlas and partition up to equivalent norms; the atlas-independence lemma on this page proves the invariance.

Well-definedness on classes follows from the Euclidean representative independence, and atlas independence is proved separately in [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]]. items.title: Chart independence of the fractional boundary norm
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded
$C^1$ domain, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$.

(i) If $\Psi:V\to V'$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism between open subsets of
$\mathbb R^{d}$, $d\ge1$, which is bi-Lipschitz and whose derivatives in both directions are bounded,
then for every measurable $u:V'\to\mathbb K$,
$$\|u\circ\Psi\|_{W^{s,p}(V)}\le C(\Psi,s,p)\,\|u\|_{W^{s,p}(V')}$$
and symmetrically with $\Psi^{-1}$; in particular the Slobodeckij norm
$\|\cdot\|_{W^{s,p}}$ of [[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]]
is preserved up to equivalence by such coordinate changes. Here the norm on an open set uses the same double integral restricted to that set, with its $L^p$ term. Bounded derivatives alone on arbitrary open sets do not imply the bi-Lipschitz hypothesis.

(ii) Consequently two finite boundary chart families with subordinate
partitions, as in
[[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], define
equivalent norms on $\partial\Omega$: the sum norms differ by multiplicative
constants depending only on the two atlases, the dimension and $s,p$, so
$W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega)$ is well defined as a set and its topology is
atlas-independent.
items.strategy: Assume global bi-Lipschitz bounds for the general coordinate-change assertion and change variables in both integral factors with bounded inverse Jacobians. For atlas overlaps obtain local bi-Lipschitz bounds on small balls, apply bounded Lipschitz multipliers and positive-support-margin zero extension, then sum finitely and reverse the atlases.

items.title: The half-space trace lies in the fractional Slobodeckij space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, $H=\mathbb R^d\times(0,\infty)$, and let $T_+$ be the half-space trace of [[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]]. Then for every $u\in W^{1,p}(H)$ with $g=T_+u$, $[g]_{\theta,p}^p\le C(d,p)\bigl(\|u\|_{L^p(H)}^p+\|\partial_nu\|_{L^p(H)}^p\bigr)\le C(d,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p$; equivalently $T_+:W^{1,p}(H)\to W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ is bounded. The estimate is invariant under the half-space scaling $(x',t)\mapsto(rx',rt)$ in the sense that both sides scale with the same exponent.
items.strategy: Prove the estimate first for $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ (viewed on $\overline H$) and write $f=u(\cdot,0)$. By the triangle inequality, $|f(x'+h')-f(x')|\le|f(x'+h')-u(x'+h'/2,|h'|/2)|+|f(x')-u(x'+h'/2,|h'|/2)|$. Substituting $x'+h'\mapsto y'$ and then $h'\mapsto-h'$ shows that the two terms have equal integrals, so it suffices to bound the second one. The Leibniz-Newton formula along the segment from $(x',0)$ to $(x'+h'/2,|h'|/2)$ bounds it by $\int_0^{|h'|}|Du(x'+t(h'/|h'|),t)|dt$. Polar coordinates in $h'$ and Hardy's inequality [[lem-one-dimensional-hardy-inequality-on-the-half-line]] in the radius variable reduce the resulting expression to $\int_{H}|Du|^p$, with the weight $|h'|^{-(n-1)-p(1-1/p)}$ supplied by the exponent identity $p-1=p\theta$. For general $u\in W^{1,p}(H)$ approximate by restrictions of $C_c^\infty$ functions ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]); the traces converge in $L^p$ and the estimate passes to the limit by Fatou along an a.e.-convergent subsequence. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density interface.

items.title: A bounded right inverse of the half-space trace by normal mollification
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$. Fix
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varphi=1$, put
$\varphi_t(y):=t^{-d}\varphi(y/t)$ for $t>0$ and
$\psi:=-\sum_i\partial_i(y_i\varphi)$, so that $\int\psi=0$ and
$\partial_t(g*\varphi_t)=t^{-1}(g*\psi_t)$; fix
$\eta\in C_c^\infty([0,\infty))$ with $\eta\equiv1$ on $[0,1]$ and
$\eta\equiv0$ on $[2,\infty)$. For $g\in W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ define
$$R_+g(x,t):=\eta(t)\,(g*\varphi_t)(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d,\ t>0.$$
Then $R_+g\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^d\times(0,\infty))$ with
$$\partial_t(R_+g)=\eta'(t)(g*\varphi_t)+\eta(t)t^{-1}(g*\psi_t),\qquad \partial_{x_i}(R_+g)=\eta(t)(g*\partial_i\varphi_t),$$
and $\|R_+g\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C(d,p,\varphi,\eta)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d)}$.
Moreover $T_+(R_+g)=g$, so $R_+$ is a bounded linear right inverse of the
half-space trace $T_+$.
items.strategy: Differentiate the scaled kernel exactly; normal and tangential derivatives are t^(-1) times scaled mean-zero kernels. Their scale estimate and cutoff bounds control W1p. Fractional smooth density and Sobolev completeness identify the convolution limit and its derivatives; trace continuity gives the right-inverse identity.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A chart-supported power singularity has finite Lp norm and divergent directional fractional integral, proving strictness. A normalised concentrating family has bounded W1p lifts, fractional traces bounded below and Lp traces tending to zero, proving noncompactness.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, and let $T$ be the trace. The right inverse is not unique and no canonical choice is claimed.

items.title: Inhomogeneous Dirichlet data reduce to zero trace
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, and let $R$ be the right inverse of [[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]]. Then for every $g\in W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ and every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ with $Tu=g$ one has $u=Rg+v$ with $v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and conversely every such $u=Rg+v$ has trace $g$. If $g_0\in L^p(\partial\Omega)\setminus W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$, a set nonempty for $p>1$, then no $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ satisfies $Tu=g_0$: the inhomogeneous problem is solvable exactly for data in the trace range, not for arbitrary boundary $L^p$ data.
items.strategy: Compute $T(u-Rg)=Tu-T(Rg)=g-g=0$, so $v:=u-Rg$ lies in the kernel of $T$, which equals $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ by [[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]]. Conversely, $T(Rg+v)=T(Rg)+Tv=g+0=g$. The final statement is the definition of the range of $T$ combined with the strictness clause of [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]]. No choice beyond the cited interfaces is used.

items.title: Endpoint and rough-domain limitations of the trace theorems
items.statement: Scope and limitations of the trace theory of this page. (i) The sharp range statement is proved for $1<p<\infty$; at $p=1$ the trace operator $T:W^{1,1}(\Omega)\to L^1(\partial\Omega)$ is still bounded and onto, but $L^1(\partial\Omega)$ must not be renamed $W^{0,1}(\partial\Omega)$, and there is no bounded linear right inverse $L^1(\partial\Omega)\to W^{1,1}(\Omega)$; the $p=1$ surjectivity of Gagliardo and the nonexistence of a bounded linear extension are cited here, not proved on this page. (ii) The trace theorems use bounded $C^1$ domains with the local one-sided graph property of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], without uniform constants across all charts or domains. Compact patches and a finite boundary cover give domain-dependent derivative bounds. Individual $C^1$ arcs do not suffice at an outward-cusp tip, where the local graph property fails. For the planar model $\Omega_\alpha=\{(x,y):0<y<1, |x|<y^\alpha\}$ the companion concentrating sequence disproves the unweighted $W^{1,p}$ to boundary $L^p$ bound for $\alpha>p$. Weighted estimates require their own hypotheses; neither necessity of weighting nor a universal cusp threshold is asserted. (iii) Gagliardo's original hypotheses are Lipschitz, not $C^1$, and the same statements hold for bounded Lipschitz domains with the Lipschitz boundary atlas; the $C^1$ version proved here is a special case, and no Lipschitz-domain strengthening beyond finite-dimensional Euclidean domains is claimed. (iv) The zero-boundary identification $\ker T=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ is used only as a statement about the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no pointwise boundary parametrisation of an arbitrary Sobolev class is claimed.
items.strategy: This is a scope remark: every assertion is either a proved statement of this page cited through the dependency list or an explicitly attributed classical fact recorded with its source in the reference list. The $p=1$ surjectivity is Gagliardo's Teorema [1.II] as reproved by Mironescu, and the absence of a bounded linear right inverse at $p=1$ is Peetre's theorem as quoted by Hajlasz and Martio. The outward-cusp limitation is documented by Zuppa and by the weighted-space literature he cites. No proof is supplied for the attributed endpoint facts, and no choice principle beyond the cited interfaces is used.

title: Sobolev Traces and Zero Boundary Values — Examples

items.title: The trace of a one-dimensional Sobolev function is the pair of endpoint values
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $I=(a,b)$ be a bounded interval, $1\le p<\infty$
and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Identify the boundary
$\partial I=\{a,b\}$ with its counting measure, so that
$L^p(\partial I;\mathbb K)=\mathbb K^2$ with the norm
$(|z_a|^p+|z_b|^p)^{1/p}$. For $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ let $u^*$ be its
unique absolutely continuous representative
([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]])
and define the **trace**
$$Tu:=\bigl(u^*(a),u^*(b)\bigr)\in\mathbb K^2.$$
Then $T:W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)\to\mathbb K^2$ is a well-defined linear bounded
operator depending only on the class of $u$; and
$$u\in W_0^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Tu=(0,0),$$
where $W_0^{1,p}(I)$ is the $W^{1,p}$-closure of $C_c^\infty(I)$
([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). On $I=(0,1)$ the function
$u(x)=x(1-x)$ has $u^*=u$, $Tu=(0,0)$ and lies in $W_0^{1,p}(0,1)$, while
$u\equiv1$ has $Tu=(1,1)\ne0$ and lies outside $W_0^{1,p}(0,1)$.
items.strategy: Bound the endpoint pair using the AC representative. For vanishing endpoints choose cutoffs with interior support and control their derivative error by the local integral of |u prime|^p. Zero extension and smooth approximation with tolerance adjusted to the multiplier norm yield tests. Trace continuity gives the converse.

items.title: The trace of an affine function on a ball is its classical restriction
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega=B_R(0)\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, $1\le p<\infty$, $c\in\mathbb R^n$, $d\in\mathbb K$, and $u(x)=c\cdot x+d$. Then $u\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ and, by [[lem-sobolev-trace-agrees-with-continuous-boundary-values]], $Tu=(c\cdot x+d)|_{\partial\Omega}$; moreover $Tu\in W^{1-1/p,p}(\partial\Omega)$ with $\|Tu\|_{W^{1-1/p,p}(\partial\Omega)}\le C(R,n,p)(|c|R+|d|)$ by [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]]. On the circle $\partial B_R(0)$, $\|Tu\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}^p=R^{n-1}\int_{S^{n-1}}|c\cdot R\omega+d|^p d\sigma(\omega)$, which is the classical surface integral of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]].
items.strategy: The function is smooth up to the compact boundary, so its trace is its classical restriction by [[lem-sobolev-trace-agrees-with-continuous-boundary-values]] and its tangential derivatives are bounded by $|c|$; the fractional membership follows from [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]] applied to the constant control $\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(B_R)}\le C(R,n,p)(|c|R+|d|)$. The displayed $L^p$ value is the chart-integral formula for the sphere. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the trace interface used.

items.title: Boundary point values are not a function of the interior $L^p$ class
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. The following two claims are false. (1) On a bounded
$C^1$ domain $\Omega$, boundary values are a function of the interior class:
for every $L^p(\Omega)$ class the pointwise boundary values of a
representative are determined by the class, so that classical restriction
would descend to $L^p(\Omega)$. (2) Every $L^p(\Omega)$ class is bounded near
$\partial\Omega$, so that pointwise evaluation on $\partial\Omega$ could be
recovered from the interior class. In fact two functions with the same
interior class can have different classical boundary restrictions, and a
single $L^2$ class can be unbounded on every neighbourhood of the boundary;
the Sobolev trace is defined on $W^{1,p}$ classes and does not assign a
trace to every $L^p$ class.
items.strategy: The coincidence of the two classes is the definition of $L^p$ as a quotient by null functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and the fact that $\partial\Omega$ is a Lebesgue-null set with empty interior. The classical restrictions differ at every boundary point, since $\tilde f|_{\partial\Omega}\equiv1$. The trace of both classes vanishes because the defining clause of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] gives $T$ applied to the continuous function $0$. The unbounded example is the standard $L^2$ function $(1-|x|)^{-1/4}$ on the unit ball, whose $L^2$ norm is finite while no neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega$ has a finite essential bound. No choice beyond Countable Choice is used.

items.title: A jump boundary datum is outside the trace range for $p\ge2$
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. The claim that for $p\ge2$ every boundary datum
$g\in L^p(\partial\Omega)$ on a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$
is the trace of some $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ is false. Let a boundary chart
containing the closed straight segment $[0,1]$ strictly inside its patch be given and let $g=\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}$
be the jump function on that segment, extended by zero. Then
$g\in L^p(\partial\Omega)$ for every $p$, but for every $2\le p<\infty$ one has
$g\notin W^{1-1/p,p}(\partial\Omega)$: the chart computation gives a divergent
Slobodeckij seminorm, and by
[[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]] no $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ has $Tu=g$.
In particular the Dirichlet datum is not arbitrary in $L^p(\partial\Omega)$,
and the trace range depends on $p$: for $1<p<2$ the same jump function does
belong to $W^{1-1/p,p}(\partial\Omega)$ because $1-1/p<1/p$.
items.strategy: Integrate both outside half-lines for the indicator of (0,1), obtaining (4/(p theta))∫_0^1 x^(-p theta)dx. Put the closed segment strictly inside a straight chart and transfer by cutoffs and atlas equivalence. The threshold p theta=p-1=1 separates finite and divergent seminorms.

items.title: Zero trace, zero boundary values and zero extension agree on an interval
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $I=(0,1)$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ with absolutely continuous representative $u^*$
([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]]),
and let $T$ be the endpoint-pair trace of
[[ex-trace-of-an-ac-sobolev-function-on-an-interval]]. The following four
statements are equivalent:

(i) $Tu=0$;

(ii) $u^*(0)=u^*(1)=0$;

(iii) $u\in W_0^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$, the $W^{1,p}$-closure of
$C_c^\infty(I)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]);

(iv) the extension of $u$ by zero outside $I$ belongs to
$W^{1,p}(\mathbb R;\mathbb K)$.

For $u(x)=x(1-x)$ all four hold: the zero extension is the continuous function
equal to $x(1-x)$ on $[0,1]$ and to $0$ outside, with weak derivative $1-2x$ on
$(0,1)$ and $0$ outside. For $u\equiv1$ all four fail: $Tu=(1,1)\ne0$, and the
zero extension cannot belong to $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R)$ by the implication proved
in step 1.2 below.
items.strategy: (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii) is the one-dimensional trace identification of [[ex-trace-of-an-ac-sobolev-function-on-an-interval]]. (ii)$\Leftrightarrow$(iv): the zero extension is absolutely continuous across the endpoints exactly when both endpoint values vanish, and then its derivative is the zero extension of $u'$, so the ACL characterisation [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]] gives membership in $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R)$. (ii)$\Rightarrow$(iii): cut off $u$ by a fixed interior cutoff $\eta_\delta$ equal to one on $[\delta,1-\delta]$; the endpoint vanishing gives $\|u(1-\eta_\delta)\|_{W^{1,p}(I)}\to0$ because $|u(x)|\le x^{1-1/p}\|u'\|_{L^p}$ near an endpoint, and the compactly supported pieces are approximated by test functions using [[lem-compact-support-zero-extension-in-wkp]] and mollification. (iii)$\Rightarrow$(ii): test functions have both endpoint values zero and the endpoint pairing is continuous, so the property passes to the closure. The two concrete functions are checked by direct differentiation: $x(1-x)$ vanishes at both endpoints, while $\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}$ has the displayed Dirac derivative by integration by parts against test functions (the companion PDE-12 counterexample records the computation). Countable Choice is carried by the ACL and extension interfaces.

items.title: The trace estimate fails on an outward cusp above the critical sharpness
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $1\le p<\infty$, let $\alpha>p$, and put
$$\Omega_\alpha:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:0<y<1,\ |x|<y^\alpha\},$$
a bounded open set with an outward cusp at the origin whose boundary consists
of the two $C^1$ arcs $x=\pm y^\alpha$ ($0<y<1$), the cusp point $(0,0)$, and the top segment
$y=1$, $|x|\le1$, and which carries finite surface measure. Then there is no
bounded linear operator $S:W^{1,p}(\Omega_\alpha)\to L^p(\partial\Omega_\alpha)$
that agrees with classical restriction on $C^1(\overline\Omega_\alpha)$: for
$\theta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with $\theta\equiv1$ on $[-1,1]$ and
$\theta\equiv0$ on $[2,\infty)$ and $u_\delta(x,y):=\theta(y/\delta)$ one has
$u_\delta\in W^{1,p}(\Omega_\alpha)$ with
$\|u_\delta\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega_\alpha)}^p\le C\,\delta^{\alpha+1-p}$ and
$\|u_\delta|_{\partial\Omega_\alpha}\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega_\alpha)}^p\ge2\delta$,
so the ratio
$\|u_\delta|_{\partial\Omega_\alpha}\|/\|u_\delta\|_{W^{1,p}}$ diverges like
$\delta^{(p-\alpha)/p}\to\infty$ as $\delta\downarrow0$. Consequently the
hypothesis that $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^1$ domain in the uniform graph sense
of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] cannot be relaxed to
arbitrary bounded open sets whose boundary pieces are merely $C^1$ curves;
this witness refutes the unweighted estimate and asserts no weighted replacement theorem.
items.strategy: For u_delta=theta(y/delta), compute interior norm power comparable to delta^(alpha+1-p) and regular-arc boundary norm power comparable to delta. A nonzero derivative subinterval gives the interior lower bound. The ratio delta^((p-alpha)/p) diverges for alpha>p, contradicting any bounded restriction extension. The cusp point needs no regular surface chart; no weighted replacement is asserted.

items.title: A Poisson-type extension and its local and global Sobolev traces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $d\ge1$ and use the $2\pi$-normalised Fourier
transform. For $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$ define
$$U(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{2\pi ix\cdot\xi}e^{-2\pi t|\xi|}\widehat g(\xi)\,d\xi,\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d,\ t\ge0.$$
Then $U$ is smooth on $\mathbb R^d\times[0,\infty)$, bounded and harmonic on
$H=\mathbb R^d\times(0,\infty)$, extends the datum with $U(\cdot,0)=g$, and
$\nabla U\in L^2(H)$ with
$$\|\nabla U\|_{L^2(H)}^2=2\pi\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\xi|\,|\widehat g(\xi)|^2\,d\xi<\infty.$$
The classical boundary value is realised by the trace in two forms. (i) For
every $R>0$, choose $\kappa_R\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ equal to one on
$B_R(0)$ and a smooth compact normal cutoff $\eta$ equal to one near zero.
Then $V_R(x,t)=\kappa_R(x)\eta(t)U(x,t)$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(H)$, is
continuous with compact support in $\overline H$, and
$T_+V_R=\kappa_Rg$, giving the boundary value on $B_R(0)$.
(ii) If in
addition $U\in L^2(H)$ — which holds for every $g$ when $d\ge2$, and for
$d=1$ exactly when $\int_{\mathbb R}g=0$ — then $U\in W^{1,2}(H)$ and
$T_+U=g$ for the flat trace $T_+$ of
[[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]]. For $d=1$ with
$\int_{\mathbb R}g\ne0$ one has $U\notin L^2(H)$, so the half-space trace is
not defined on $U$ and (i) is the correct local form of the identity. This
exhibits a Poisson-type right inverse of the half-space trace for smooth data satisfying the stated $L^2$ condition; the cutoff form
gives a local lift for every smooth datum. It is an illustration only: it does not prove the general-$p$ right
inverse of [[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]].
items.strategy: Differentiate the Fourier integral using Schwartz decay. Apply integral/L2 agreement and Plancherel to the L1∩L2 derivative symbols, sum and integrate to obtain 2 pi∫|xi||g hat|^2. Compact spatial/normal cutoffs give local traces. The global L2 norm equals (4 pi)^(-1)∫|g hat|^2/|xi|, finite for d≥2 or d=1 with zero mean; under that condition cutoff convergence yields the global trace.
